surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the reduction of WF6 by silane (SiH4), leading to the formation of tungsten (W) and by-products such as SiF4 and H2. The process is self-limiting, with the surface reaction dynamics monitored through real-time mass spectrometry (QMS) signals. During the SiH4 half-cycle, the by-product H2 is generated from the surface reaction between silane and adsorbed W species, while during the WF6 half-cycle, the by-product SiF4 is generated. The QMS signals for these by-products decrease after saturation, indicating the completion of the surface reactions.
